For this repository, I would like to set up the following:

04
Connect your repository
Sign in
Everyone on the team signs in to Entire with Sign in with GitHub and authorizes the Entire GitHub App when prompted. You can do this at any time, before or after the next step.

GitHub organization admin: import the repository
A GitHub organization admin installs the Entire GitHub App on the organization by following the onboarding. Nothing repository-related appears for anyone in the team until this step is done.

Sign-in order doesn't matter, but the repository and its sessions only show up after the admin has configured access.

Once the admin has imported the repository, it appears for the whole team. No invites and no permission setup: access follows the GitHub collaborator list, so everyone keeps the same roles they have on GitHub.

Changes can take up to an hour to sync. If the repository is missing from your list, ask your organization admin.
Next: install the CLI and start your first checkpoint (following section).

05
Push your first agent session
Install Entire, then enable it from your repository
Shell

Copy
# macOS/Linux:
curl -fsSL https://entire.io/install.sh | bash

# Windows:
irm https://entire.io/install.ps1 | iex

cd your-repo
entire enable
Work as normal by starting a new agent session, ask your agent to make a focused change, and review the result.

Commit the change
Shell

Copy
git add path/to/changed-file
git commit -m "Build my first feature with Entire"
Choose yes if prompted to link the commit to session context.

Inspect your checkpoint
Shell

Copy
entire checkpoint list
entire checkpoint explain HEAD

I recommend enabling Entire for Codex first, using this repository’s existing GitHub remote.

I checked the local setup: the working tree is clean, `origin` points to `schwarbf/planworldsimulator`, Entire is absent from `PATH`, and there are no active Git hooks. Nothing has been changed.

1. **Connect GitHub in Entire.** Sign in with GitHub, then install or configure the Entire GitHub App for `schwarbf/planworldsimulator`. Verify whether `schwarbf` is a personal account or organization; the onboarding you pasted specifically describes organizations. Select only this repository initially.

2. **Install the stable CLI and authenticate.**
   ```sh
   curl -fsSL https://entire.io/install.sh | bash
   entire version
   entire login
   ```

3. **Enable capture in this repository.** Check the installed version’s help, then configure Codex:
   ```sh
   cd /Users/florianschwarb/code/personal/planworldsimulator
   entire enable --help
   entire enable --agent codex --telemetry=false
   entire status
   ```
   Entire creates repository settings and installs Git and agent hooks. These commands follow the [current CLI documentation](https://github.com/entireio/cli#quick-start).

4. **Review the generated configuration.** Inspect the diff, commit shared `.entire/settings.json` and any required agent configuration, and ensure local settings and runtime data stay ignored. Add a short README note explaining that each teammate must install Entire and enable hooks in their own clone. Use `origin` for checkpoints initially; confirm repository visibility before uploading session transcripts.

5. **Create the first captured checkpoint.** Start a fresh Codex session after enabling hooks, make a small useful change, review it, and commit the relevant files. Choose yes when prompted to link session context. Verify:
   ```sh
   entire checkpoint list
   entire checkpoint explain HEAD
   git show -s --format=%B HEAD
   ```
   Success means the checkpoint contains the session and the commit has an `Entire-Checkpoint` trailer. [Checkpoint documentation](https://github.com/entireio/cli#checkpoints)

6. **Push and verify in Entire.** Push the reviewed commit to GitHub, then confirm its session appears in Entire. Allow the sync time described in your onboarding. Repeat local installation and enablement for teammates.

The main point to verify during setup is capture from your actual Codex client. An enabled status alone is insufficient; the first checkpoint must contain the session transcript.

I want to enable codex and claude code here, how can I do this? I downloaded and logged into entire now

entire enable --help
Enable Entire with session tracking for your AI agent workflows.

If Entire is not yet configured, this runs the full configuration flow.
If Entire is already configured but disabled, this re-enables it.

If the current directory is not a git repository, Entire can initialize one
for you and create an initial commit. It never creates or pushes to a remote —
publish the repository yourself when you're ready.

Usage:
  entire enable [flags]

Flags:
      --absolute-git-hook-path               Embed full binary path in git hooks (for GUI git clients that don't source shell profiles)
      --agent string                         Agent to set up hooks for (e.g., antigravity, claude-code, codex, copilot-cli, cursor, factoryai-droid, opencode, pi; external agents on $PATH are also available). Enables non-interactive mode.
      --agent-help-skill entire agent-help   Install the stable Entire agent-help skill (points agents at entire agent-help) for selected agent(s)
      --checkpoint-backend string            Checkpoint storage backend: refs (default; one git ref per checkpoint) or branch (legacy shared entire/checkpoints/v1 branch)
      --checkpoint-push-remote string        Git remote for checkpoint uploads (saved to .entire/settings.local.json, even with --project)
      --checkpoint-remote string             Checkpoint remote in provider:owner/repo format; providers: github, gitlab (e.g., github:org/checkpoints-repo)
  -f, --force                                Force reinstall hooks (removes existing Entire hooks first)
  -h, --help                                 help for enable
      --import-history                       During first-time setup, import the selected agents' existing session history (last 30 days) without prompting
      --init-repo                            If not a git repo, initialize one non-interactively
      --initial-commit-message string        Commit message for the initial commit when bootstrapping a new repo
      --local                                Write settings to .entire/settings.local.json instead of .entire/settings.json
      --no-init-repo                         If not a git repo, exit instead of prompting to initialize one
      --project                              Write settings to .entire/settings.json even if it already exists
      --search-skill                         Install the optional Entire search skill for selected agent(s)
      --skip-initial-commit                  Don't create the initial commit when bootstrapping a new repo
      --skip-push-sessions                   Disable automatic pushing of session logs on git push
      --telemetry                            Enable anonymous usage analytics (default true)
  -y, --yes                                  Accept all defaults without prompting (in a non-repo directory: init git and commit; then enable all agents and accept telemetry). Does not import existing agent history — see --import-history

Global Flags:
      --context name   Act as this saved login name for this command only — including the git and agent processes it spawns — instead of the active context (entire auth contexts lists them)

Run these commands here to enable Codex, then add Claude Code:

```sh
cd /Users/florianschwarb/code/personal/planworldsimulator

entire enable --agent codex --telemetry=false --absolute-git-hook-path
entire agent add claude-code

entire agent list
entire status
```

I verified these commands against your installed CLI. `--absolute-git-hook-path` helps Git hooks find Entire when commits come from a GUI client; `--telemetry=false` disables anonymous usage analytics.

Then start **fresh Codex and Claude Code sessions** in this repository. After making and reviewing a focused change, commit it and accept the session-linking prompt. Check capture with:

```sh
entire checkpoint list
entire checkpoint explain HEAD
```

Review the generated files before committing the setup. Each teammate needs to install Entire and enable their own local hooks too.
